disease_label_per_paper: Ruptured tubo-ovarian abscess complicated by sepsis and extraperitoneal spillage
presentation_summary: 43-year-old sexually active woman presented to the emergency room in shock with severe abdominal pain.
Pain was widespread and especially involved the right iliac and lumbar regions, with anorexia and vomiting; movement aggravated the pain.
She had low-grade fever for a week and chronic abdominal pain for a month with gradual worsening.
On admission she appeared ill and tachypneic; vital signs were temperature 100.4 F, pulse 130/min, and blood pressure 88/56 mmHg.
Examination showed guarding and lower abdominal/right lumbar tenderness and a large firm pelvic mass extending from the pelvis to the umbilicus.
Labs showed WBC 29,430/mm3, hemoglobin 5.3 g/dL, platelets 488,000/mm3, CRP 19.38 mg/dL, and procalcitonin 1.52 ng/mL.
CT abdomen and pelvis revealed a hypodense collection in the right adnexa extending to the right iliac fossa and dissecting into the right rectus sheath plane of the anterior abdominal wall.

quality_warnings: Operative rupture confirmation, pus culture, treatment response, and discharge outcome are confirmatory/non-ranking.
